A1.justification: Both PDFs describe OpenGround and OpenTarget. All 27 pages of v1 and 46 pages of v3, including appendices, references, equations, tables, and figures, support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original grounding experiments, component ablations, a human task-ordering study, and additional quantitative and qualitative evaluations in its appendix.

after.justification: v3 retains original experiments and reports additional baseline comparisons, component ablations, and an audit of intermediate grounding errors.

M1.justification: Beyond renaming, v3 changes inference procedures. Section 5.1 and Table 13 relax v1's mandatory target-last ordering. Section 10.3 and Algorithm 2 replace candidate-priority view selection with context-based candidate rejection followed by joint coverage selection. Section 10.2 also specifies proposal-box IoU merging, whereas v1 Section 4.2 specifies point-mask IoU merging.

E1.justification: Coverage remains OpenTarget, ScanRefer, and Nr3D, plus qualitative ScanNet++ and Toronto3D applications already present in v1's appendix. OpenTarget retains 7,724 queries and the same object/part coverage. New difficulty strata, model configurations, and diagnostic samples do not introduce a different dataset or grounding task.

E2.justification: v3 Tables 1, 7, and 9 add OpenTarget comparisons with ZSVG3D, SPAZER, 3D-R1, GS-Reasoner, and TSP3D; several appeared only on other benchmarks in v1. Table 6 adds comparisons between SeeGround, SeqVLM, and Struct2D view selectors. Conversely, the ScanRefer method row in v1 Table 1 is absent from v3 Table 2.

E3.justification: v3 Tables 2–3 introduce broader comparisons matching OpenGround's VLM to baseline backbones, replacing its single GLM-4.5V ScanRefer configuration and expanding Nr3D configurations. OpenTarget gains quantitative Mask3D baseline controls and hierarchy-based Easy/Hard strata containing 5,737/1,987 queries. The new error audit samples 50 failed and 50 successful cases. These change evaluation design within retained coverage.

E4.justification: v3 Table 6 adds isolated view-selector comparisons and ablations of condition decomposition and unannotated images, extending v1's annotation and whole-backbone tests. Section 13 adds an intermediate-error audit, and Figure 2 adds cross-dataset complexity analysis. The chain-length curves, ground-truth OLT experiment, and segmentation-backbone comparisons already existed in v1's appendix.

E5.justification: v3 Section 5.1 newly reports uncertainty alongside existing WAED means: 0.90 ± 0.49 for the planner and 0.63 ± 0.29 for human disagreement. v1 Figures 4 and 10 report point estimates only. Neither PDF establishes additional repeated grounding runs, seed reporting, or significance testing.

E6.justification: v3 adds extensive backbone-specific, subgroup, baseline, and diagnostic results, including SPAZER with GT OLT at 39.2/28.7 on OpenTarget. OpenGround's 46.2/34.2 remains unchanged. The ScanRefer GLM result of 61.8/53.1 is replaced by other configurations, including GPT-4o at 64.5/55.9, not a same-setting gain. Annotation-ablation entries change from 20.3 to 25.3 for all objects and 28.8 to 26.5 for candidates only, alongside the revised grounding procedure. v1's GLM Nr3D rows disappear.

T1.justification: v3 relaxes the formal target-last restriction accompanying v1 Equation 4 and introduces explicit depth-consistency visibility and proposal-box overlap definitions in Equations 10–14. The WAED definitions and core greedy coverage equations are retained. Neither version provides theoretical guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: The central claims remain compatible zero-shot grounding beyond a predefined OLT through progressive task chains and dynamic perception, introduction of OpenTarget, and strong benchmark performance. Both abstracts retain the same Nr3D, ScanRefer, and 17.6% OpenTarget headline claims. The cognition-to-planning terminology shift mainly reframes these retained contributions.

C2.justification: v3 Section 9 develops an argument for OLT as persistent memory and for demand-driven completion, while v1's representation-agnostic cognition discussion disappears. v3 newly explains smaller closed-set gains and interprets the error audit as evidence that cascading errors are not dominant. Existing static-scene, proximity, and segmentation limitations remain, with added confidence-based remedies. The earlier API-throttling caveat for runtime comparisons is removed.

D1.justification: v3 discloses 41 participants and 410 annotations, dataset filtering and rewriting counts, 20-frame sampling with approximately 56 views per scene, visibility/backprojection details, grounding temperature 0.2, and SPAZER reproduction parameters. It adds a project-page link. These are mostly new disclosures, not evidence of changed existing runs. However, v1's candidate threshold of 0.9 disappears, and v3's stated 95% coverage stopping rule conflicts with Algorithm 1's full-coverage condition.

R1.justification: v3 substantially expands positioning around offline OLT methods, OLT completion, and OLT-free approaches. It adds discussions of AffordBot, GS-Reasoner, ConceptFusion, and OpenScene, and attributes greedy view selection to Video-3D LLM. The ThinkInSpace/cognitive-map connection and several citations disappear. These changes revise the relationship to prior research beyond reference formatting.

P1.justification: The title and module terminology change throughout, and the introduction, related work, and method narrative are extensively rewritten. A new Preliminary section separates the existing grounding paradigm; Single-Step Grounding moves into the appendix. The added OLT discussion, rewritten planning prompt, and reorganized experimental and limitations sections substantially change the narrative structure.

P2.justification: v3 changes the predominantly two-column layout to a single-column format, redraws major introduction and method diagrams, and restructures benchmark tables with VLM groupings and Easy/Hard columns. v1 Figure 12's chain-length plots move into v3 Figure 8; backbone bars are redrawn beside Table 4. New component-ablation and supervised-comparison tables accompany these extensive visual changes.

improvement.justification: Matched-VLM comparisons, broader OpenTarget controls and baselines, isolated component ablations, and the error audit strengthen empirical support and attribution. Added study and implementation details also improve transparency. The net gain is limited by inconsistencies: the retained 17.6% headline does not reflect the stronger added SPAZER comparison, and the new 95% coverage rule disagrees with Algorithm 1. The revision improves evidential quality while leaving important reporting and reproducibility questions unresolved.
